item.title: Connecting Threads (together): Textile Works by Lynn Setterington — Tue Sep 29, 12:00 PM — UC Davis Design Museum
item.description:
The UC Davis Design Museum opens its 2026-2027 season with Connecting Threads (together): Textile Works by Lynn Setterington which opens on Sept. 29 and runs through Nov. 20. Collaboration is at the heart of textile making and this idea is explored in a display of work by UK based artist Setterington. Through textiles the artist challenges contemporary issues in society and how stitch can be used to commemorate people and communities. She has worked with underserved communities across the globe, including the UK, India, Bangladesh, Brazil and USA. She draws on popular culture and textile history to raise awareness of societal issues. Themes range from sustainability, place, well-being and identity and belonging. This exhibition is co-sponsored by the Maria Manetti Shrem Institute for Sustainable Design, Fashion & Textiles.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Yolo Co. Voter Forum — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — Richard Brunelle Performance Hall
item.description:
by: Lorna Carriveau, League of Women Voters
League of Women Voters Forums Coming Soon
The League of Women Voters of Yolo County will be hosting multiple public, nonpartisan forums in September and October in advance of the general election on November 3.
The League’s first forum in Davis, on Thursday, Sep. 30, will be a nonpartisan voter education forum focusing on Proposition 39. Proposition 39, known as the Prohibit Voting Without Government-Issued ID initiative, aims to require all voters in California to present government-issued identification when they submit their ballot and to prove U.S. citizenship at the time they register to vote. This initiative is designed to create a new voter ID requirement and a new citizenship documentation process for voter registration. Proposition 39 increases the documentation requirements for eligible citizens to participate in elections in an effort to prevent non-citizen voting.

item.description:

Speaker: Sheena Campbell & Michele Tobias
UC Davis STEM Librarian, Sheena Campbell, provides information literacy instruction to undergraduate and professional students in the STEM fields, offers individualized research support, and identifies resources to enhance the library’s collections. With her background as an artist and historian, Sheena’s research interests focus on the intersection of visual culture, environmental justice, and the history of scientific thought.

item.title: Banned Books Week — Sun Oct 4 — CA
item.description:
Banned Books Week was launched in 1982 in response to a sudden surge in the number of challenges to books in libraries, bookstores, and schools. Held in the last week of September or first week of October, the annual event highlights the value of free and open access to information and brings together the entire book community — librarians, educators, authors, publishers, booksellers, and readers of all types — in shared support of the freedom to seek and to express ideas. The next Banned Books Week will be held October 4–10, 2026. The theme of this year’s event is: Let Books Be — Protect the Freedom to Read.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: maptimeDavis: Augmented Reality (AR) Mapping — Fri Oct 16, 10:00 AM — DataLab Classsroom
item.description:
Learn how augmented reality (AR) tools can be used for education and research! We'll visit DataLab's AR Sandbox for a fun (and educational) experience with AR tools.
Speaker: Oliver Kreylos
Oliver Kreylos is a computer scientist researching virtual reality and computer graphics, and their application to scientific data analysis. Kreylos received his PhD in Computer Science from UC Davis. He holds master’s degrees in Computer Science from UC Davis and the University of Karlsruhe, Germany. Kreylos developed the virtual reality user interface and research applications software for the UC Davis KeckCAVES and AR Sandbox.
Prerequisites: None
Software Required: None
Source: UC Davis Library

item.description: Claudia Dommaschk @ The Avid Reader Tuesday Sep 29th, 2026 | 6:30 PM – 7:30 PM About the Book – The Communal Heart Belonging is remembered, together. We are living in a time of profound fragmentation—within ourselves, between one another, and across the very systems meant to hold us together. In the midst of this unraveling, many of us feel the ache for belonging without knowing how to return to it. Beneath this experience lies a deeper crisis, not simply of politics or technology, but of relationship itself. We have become highly skilled at optimizing, managing, and performing. Yet in narrowing our attention toward efficiency and control, we have sacrificed the very presence that allows trust to grow. The Communal Heart offers a different starting point. item.title: Reflecting Images: Christianity and AI in Conversation — Tue Sep 29, 7:00 PM — The Episcopal Church of St. Martin
item.description: The conversation about artificial intelligence, or AI, has become a significant part of our everyday lives, to the point that so much of the current economy is bound up in this technology. It’s hard to listen to a newscast or read a headline without some mention of AI, either as ground-breaking technology that will make our lives easier and more efficient, or as a possible threat to human existence. Three local pastors have come together out of the belief that “people of faith ought to be able to think and speak intelligently about AI and navigate the many issues it involves while holding onto the values that guide them in their faith,” according to Mae Forrest Barnes, Ph.D., an Episocpalian with a background in theology and ethics and a special focus in accessibility, science, and theological ethics. item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Wed Sep 30, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.

item.title: War & Disability: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Iran and Ukraine — Tue Sep 29, 4:30 PM — International House Davis
item.description:
​As the wars in Ukraine and Iran continue to unfold, what can we learn from the experience and perspective of those with disability who are navigating the conflicts? ​The Davis Humanities Institute (DHI) is pleased to bring together leading scholars of war and disability, Professors Sarah Phillips and Sona Kazemi, for a public conversation on two of the world’s most significant, ongoing conflict zones. ​This conversation continues the DHI’s event series spotlighting interdisciplinary research on disability. The discussion will be moderated by the DHI’s Faculty Director, Professor Jenny Kaminer, and will be followed by a complimentary reception. ​Everyone welcome. Registration required (https://luma.com/imtkporv). Doors open at 4:30pm. The event will start promptly at 4:45pm.
Source: The Dirt
